title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing for partial JSON, delimiter ordering, and token/event ordering
author: Anjali Rao
description: Fixes several correctness issues in the SSE streaming encoder used by the OpenAI compatibility layer and the internal streaming runtime. Root causes addressed: (1) incorrect chunk boundaries when messages contain partial JSON objects split across token events; (2) delimiter token emission order relative to token/event frames which could lead to downstream consumers receiving out-of-order `data:` lines and partial JSON fragments; (3) race between flush on prefix cache hits and in-flight token event emission which could reorder events under high concurrency. This PR implements a deterministic framing state machine for SSE output, updates the OpenAI compat shim to preserve event ordering guarantees expected by clients, adds comprehensive unit and integration tests for partial-JSON streaming, and documents the compatibility guarantees and rollback plan. Changes are backwards-compatible for existing consumers but fix subtle cases where streamed partial JSON could not be reassembled by clients or where structured output tool-calls would receive out-of-order delimiter lines. Includes a small performance regression mitigation by batching delimiter metadata emission and deferring expensive formatting until chunk finalization. Rollout plan: feature gated behind sse_streaming_framing_v2 flag for 48-hour canary in staging then full rollout. Related Linear items: ENG-1423, ENG-2101.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Good catch on the ordering bug. Can you add a test that simulates the exact interleaving we saw in the incident?
Anjali Rao: Added deterministic interleaving tests in test_token_event_ordering_integration.py. The state machine also makes the expected ordering explicit.
Priya Singh: Small concern about potential perf cost of formatting on every token. Suggest batch formatting on chunk finalization.
Anjali Rao: Addressed by deferring heavy formatting to chunk finalization and adding microbenchmarks. Perf regression reduced to <2% in our benchmarks.
Ethan Cole: Verified OpenAI compatibility layer emits events in the order clients expect. Approving pending CI green.

release_notes: Fixes for SSE streaming framing: resolves partial-JSON reassembly bugs, ensures delimiter and token/event ordering guarantees for streaming clients, and improves stability for structured output and function-calling streams. Backwards compatible. See streaming/CHANGELOG.md for details.
snippet:
diff --git a/redwood/openai_compat/streaming.py b/redwood/openai_compat/streaming.py
--- a/redwood/openai_compat/streaming.py
+++ b/redwood/openai_compat/streaming.py
@@ -42,6 +42,22 @@ class OpenAICompatStreamer:
-    def _emit_event(self, evt):
-        # previous logic could interleave delimiter lines and token frames
-        self._raw_write(f'data: {json.dumps(evt)}\n\n')
+    def _emit_event(self, evt):
+        # write through the framing state machine to guarantee ordering
+        frame = self._framer.add(evt)
+        for line in frame.lines():
+            self._raw_write(line)
+        if frame.is_final_chunk():
+            self._raw_write('\n')
